body:
Parent: #101
Related architecture: #129 (deployment/workspace boundary), #130 (package/revision semantics), #135 (package compiler). This defect is independently reproducible and does not block those design issues from proceeding.

## Problem

A single `actions start --actions-sync=true --dir A --dir B` invocation imports both packages, then disables actions from A while synchronizing B. The repeated `--dir` arguments are parsed additively, but the per-package synchronization pass treats a sibling package's actions as omitted.

## Reproduction

Against source commit `84b8c70a412db9594dfa2a6c5fcb3e8184db019b` (Runtime 1.0.3), an isolated test creates two minimal packages, each with one action, and starts the real CLI with both directories and one shared SQLite datadir.

- Additive control: two sequential `import --dir=...` commands retain both package actions enabled (passes).
- Failing path: one `start --actions-sync=true --dir=A --dir=B` invocation logs discovery of both packages/actions, then `Disabling action: from_package_a`. The database retains both packages but reports A's action disabled and B's enabled (fails).

The exact local test command/result and source trace are retained in the convergence evidence receipt; the added regression file is test-only and was not committed to the candidate.

## Expected behavior

For one invocation with repeated `--dir` values, synchronization should treat the complete supplied directory set as desired state. An action in any supplied package remains enabled; actions from packages omitted from the full set may be disabled according to the existing sync contract.

Keep sequential import behavior and its current additive control. Add a regression for two packages in one start invocation and preserve coverage for actions genuinely omitted from the full set. Do not broaden this into managed-RCC rollback, generation atomicity, or last-good runtime behavior; those need separate evidence.

## Scope and dependencies

This is a local CLI/import synchronization defect in `action_server/src/actions/`; no upstream dependency defect is established. It does not require #129/#130/#135 to be completed first. Resolve the aggregation semantics at the local import/sync boundary, then document the verified invocation contract. No issue/PR search found an existing exact owner for the repeated-directory `actions-sync` failure.
title: Preserve sibling packages during multi-directory actions-sync startup
